proposals.text: In his autobiography, Kalindi recalls Balakrushna Kar inviting him to write a novel for Saraswat Press within two months. He wrote Matira Manisha in that period, drawing on village life; elsewhere he recognises his mother in its principal elderly woman. Writing also belonged to a working life that included textbooks, publicity and insurance. Radio later offered something he valued as an author: contact with listeners beyond the readership of his books.
proposals.footnote_text: Kalindi Charan Panigrahi, Ange Jaha Nivaichhi, second edition (Cuttack Students Store, 2006), pp.276–277,337–338,364,367–368. Original scan, Odia Bibhaba/Srujanika.

proposals.text: Kalindi also remembered advocating payment as an editor. At Bhanja Pradip, he proposed remunerating Odia writers and artists, as English contributors were paid. He recalls the proposal being accepted and receiving grateful letters. This concerned periodical contributions; his film-adaptation terms remain unverified.
proposals.footnote_text: Panigrahi, Ange Jaha Nivaichhi (2006), p.300. Original scan, Odia Bibhaba/Srujanika.
